mechanism: Core renders every scriptPubKey through ONE helper. ScriptToUniv (refs/bitcoin/src/core_io.cpp:409-428 at d3056bc) pushes asm, then desc when include_address is set (the InferDescriptor string), then hex, then address when the script is addressable and not bare PUBKEY, then type. TxToUniv calls it identically for the verbosity-3 prevout (core_io.cpp:480) and for every vout (:506), both with include_hex=true and include_address=true, so the two objects necessarily carry the same key set. We have two hand-written copies instead of one helper: output-to-json (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:510-523) emits asm, desc, hex, type and optionally address, while the prevout branch of input-to-json (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:487-503) emits asm, hex, type and optionally address -- the desc line is simply absent, and the two copies have also drifted in key ORDER. Both paths receive the same non-NIL network from tx-to-json (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:451-458), so the omission is not a missing-argument effect: scriptpubkey-desc (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:2038-2047) is available and is called for the vout on the very same call.
consequence: getblock verbosity 3, getrawtransaction verbosity 2 and any REST surface built on them return a prevout scriptPubKey missing a field Core documents as always present -- ScriptPubKeyDoc (rpc/util.cpp:1390-1398) lists desc as non-optional and rawtransaction.cpp:268 uses that doc for the prevout object, so with -rpcdoccheck (DEFAULT_RPC_DOC_CHECK) Core itself would flag the reply. A client that reads desc uniformly across vout and prevout -- an indexer resolving spent outputs to descriptors, a wallet matching prevouts against a watch descriptor -- gets a key error on the prevout half only, which is the kind of asymmetry that shows up long after integration. No wrong value is returned and no Core functional test catches it (rpc_rawtransaction.py:206-235 checks script_pub_key_fields = address/asm/hex/type as a SUBSET, and rpc_blockchain.py:690 asserts only the outer prevout key set value/height/generated/scriptPubKey), so S3. Same file, adjacent functions, one missing line.

fix_shape: Collapse the two open-coded copies into one script-to-json helper that mirrors ScriptToUniv's signature and field ORDER, and call it from both places. The helper takes the script, the network, and include-hex / include-address flags, and emits asm, then desc (only when include-address, via the existing scriptpubkey-desc), then hex, then address when addressable, then type -- which both fixes the missing desc and puts the vout's own key order back in Core's sequence. While consolidating, port the one behaviour the current copies both miss: Core suppresses the address for TxoutType::PUBKEY even though ExtractDestination succeeds (core_io.cpp:423), so a bare-pubkey output must render without an address field. Route gettxout, decodescript, getblock verbosity 2 and the REST getutxos path through the same helper so a third copy cannot appear. A regression test should assert that the prevout and vout scriptPubKey objects produced for the SAME script have identical key sets and identical desc values -- the asymmetry, not the presence of one key -- with a bare-pubkey case as the address-suppression control.
